revision_rule.note: The 2012 rule includes the longest static prefix of each variable or select expression read, but does not expressly include a plain net identifier as the 2023 rule does.
The 2017 rule includes longest-static-prefix reads of variables and select expressions, but does not include the 2023 rule's explicit coverage of each net identifier.
The 2012 exception list omits the 2023 exclusion for identifiers appearing only in wait, event, or delay timing-control expressions.
The 2017 exception list excludes block/function locals and expressions also written there, but has no exception for identifiers appearing only in timing-control expressions.
The 2012 grammar permits a bare package-scope form specifically for a sequence identifier, rather than the broader bare ps_identifier alternative in the 2023 grammar.

The 2017 grammar permits unparenthesized @ identifiers only through hierarchical-event and package/hierarchical-sequence identifier productions, rather than the 2023 generic package-scope or hierarchical identifier forms.
The 2017 rule terminates all active descendants and does not include the 2023 guarantee covering descendants whose intervening parent subprocess has already terminated.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no dynamic override specifier construct on task or function declarations.
The 2017 task and function declaration grammar has no dynamic_override_specifiers construct or corresponding declaration-scope rule.
IEEE 1800-2012 allows a process to suspend its own execution and specifies how it resumes; it does not make a function's self-suspend call an error.
The 2012 exclusion covers identifiers appearing only in wait or event expressions, but does not also exclude identifiers appearing only in delay expressions.
The 2017 exclusion covers identifiers appearing only in wait or event expressions, but unlike 2023 it does not exclude identifiers appearing only in delay expressions.
IEEE 1800-2012 permits by-reference formals in these fork forms only in fork block-item initialization expressions; it has no ref static exception.
The 2017 rule allows by-reference formals only in fork block-item initialization expressions and has no 2023 exception permitting direct references to ref static formals.
The 2012 block_item_declaration grammar additionally admits an attributed overload declaration, which the 2023 alternatives in this requirement omit.
IEEE 1800-2012 permits termination of an unblocked target at an unspecified time in the current time step and does not guarantee that all affected processes have terminated before kill() returns.
The 2017 kill() rule permits an unblocked target to terminate at an unspecified time in the current time step, rather than requiring every affected process to terminate before kill() returns.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not guarantee that kill() on an already FINISHED or KILLED target terminates its surviving descendants.
The 2017 kill() rule does not guarantee that calling kill() on a FINISHED or KILLED process terminates surviving descendants.
IEEE 1800-2012 states that kill() terminates the target and processes spawned by that target, but does not expressly extend the rule to processes spawned by those descendants.
The 2017 rule describes terminating the target and subprocesses spawned by that target; it does not include the 2023 recursive guarantee for processes spawned by descendants.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines resume() for a previously suspended process but does not guarantee that calling it in every non-SUSPENDED state has no effect.
The 2017 resume() rule does not specify that a call on every process outside SUSPENDED state has no effect.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not specify Active-or-Reactive current-time-step scheduling when resuming a process that was suspended from RUNNING.

The 2017 rule does not require an externally resumed process suspended from RUNNING to be scheduled into Active or Reactive in the current time step; it specifies only self-suspension continuation and waiting-state resensitization.
IEEE 1800-2012 permits suspension of an unblocked target at an unspecified time in the current time step and does not guarantee suspension before suspend() returns.

The 2017 rule permits suspension of an unblocked process at an unspecified time in the current time step, rather than requiring suspension before suspend() returns with the 2023 termination-race qualification.
IEEE 1800-2012 states only that repeated suspend() calls on an already suspended process have no effect; it does not extend this guarantee to FINISHED and KILLED targets.
The 2017 rule says only that repeated suspend() calls on the same suspended process have no effect; it does not extend this guarantee to FINISHED and KILLED targets.
The 2012 block_item_declaration grammar additionally admits an attributed overload declaration, which the 2023 alternatives in this requirement omit.
